threat_model: honest-but-curious seam observer of fwd seam activations h* and (in training mode) the bwd seam gradients dL/dh*, granted the victim's PUBLIC base weights (--model: embedding E + public head at --split) for auxiliary training forwards and beam verification — the BiSR/SIP white-box forward-inversion grant; the victim's finetuned head is never assumed (mismatch is part of the measurement). Canonical tokens are evaluation truth, never an attack input (label-free attack). The auxiliary training corpus is asserted article-id disjoint from the frozen validation corpus and the pilot victim corpus. Train phase: the SIP-style inverter is fit on AUXILIARY text (asserted article-disjoint from the frozen and pilot corpora) through the PUBLIC head; the victim is never queried. Aux-scale streaming path (shard cache, resume-safe).
interpretation: seq_accuracy is position-aligned vs canonical, pooled per token; bleu is smoothed corpus BLEU-4 (add-one smoothing on n>=2); token-set precision/recall are orderless per-sequence set overlaps (VFLAIR convention); the control decodes the auxiliary-corpus majority token at every position (attacker-computable; stored in the checkpoint); the gate verdict is the frozen-gate Bonferroni-Wilson excess over that control with n = scored tokens. Arm 'bisr' unions learned forward proposals with backward direction proposals and verifies by forward consistency through the public head; arm 'sip-fwd-only' is the same learned forward scores without the backward channel (the paired diagnostic); 'baseline_nn' is the position-independent cosine-NN decode over E. With --opt-arm, 'bisr_opt' is the paper's BRE second stage (SS3.2): 'b' gradient matching against the observed bwd seam gradient (Eq. 9, beta*L2+(1-beta)*L1, dummy soft labels y'=softmax(z/tau) initialized from the SIP softmax, h* fixed), 'f' smashed-data matching in the continuous embedding space (Eq. 7, cosine objective; Eq. 8 nearest-row decode), 'bf' the paper's sequential BiSR(b+f); position 0 of 'b'/'bf' comes from the SIP decode (no label gradient identifies it). A NaMoE checkpoint (--namoe, paper SS3.3) replaces the single inverter with a gating-weighted mixture of noise-aware experts; its mixture scores feed every downstream arm. This remains a PILOT-SCALE adaptation: the paper's SIP decoder is a GRU-256 trained on a substantial auxiliary corpus and NaMoE perturbs with d_XP/DP mechanisms (here: Gaussian seam noise); numbers are not comparable cell-for-cell with the paper's. Toy tier is a machinery check on synthetic seams, not a security claim.
